sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the geospatial type definitions
sections.what: Brings in the shape definitions for the policy, area sources and comparison results.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the data format checked.

sections.name: parcelAreaComparisonPolicy
sections.title: Demo tolerance policy
sections.what: Holds the policy: an identifier, a 2 percent limit for consistent, a 5 percent limit for review, and a disclaimer saying these are demo values and not legal ones.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the cut-offs in one visible place, clearly marked as not legal.
sections.watch_out: Changing these numbers changes every verdict in the demo and the test expectations.

sections.name: unitFactors
sections.title: Acre conversion table
sections.what: Lists the accepted unit names and how many acres each one equals, covering acre, hectare and square metre spellings.
sections.why: Likely reason: a lookup table is easy to read and to extend.
sections.watch_out: A unit missing from this table is rejected, so new units must be added here and in the tests.

sections.name: normalizeAreaToAcres
sections.title: Safe acre conversion
sections.what: Converts a reading into acres only if the value is a real positive number and the unit is in the table. Otherwise it returns nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a missing or invalid area is better shown as unknown than as a guessed number.
sections.watch_out: Unit names are only trimmed and lowercased before lookup, so other spelling variations are rejected.

sections.name: areaSource
sections.title: Labelled area reading
sections.what: Packages a source's raw reading together with its acre value and marks it as available or unavailable.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets later steps tell a missing reading from a real one.

sections.name: compareParcelAreas
sections.title: Pair comparison
sections.what: Compares two readings and returns the acre gap, the percentage gap and a status: consistent, review or potential issue, or insufficient evidence when either reading is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the single place where the cut-offs are applied.
sections.watch_out: The percentage uses the larger value as its base, so the result does not depend on which side is listed first.

sections.name: summarizeParcelAreaComparisons
sections.title: Overall verdict from the pairs
sections.what: Looks at the pair results and returns one overall verdict. A named hero pattern gets its own result, all consistent gives an aligned result, any missing data gives a needs-evidence result, and anything else gives a review or potential issue result.
sections.why: Likely reason: a reviewer needs one short statement, and named patterns make the demo story clear.
sections.watch_out: A new pattern is not named unless it is added here, so it falls back to the generic review result.

sections.name: compareAllParcelAreas
sections.title: Runs all three pairs and the verdict
sections.what: Finds the three area readings by source type, runs the three pair comparisons, and returns them together with the summary and the policy.
sections.why: Likely reason: one call gives the parcel view everything it needs.
sections.watch_out: The source lookup assumes each source is present, so a missing source causes an error rather than a clear message.

summary: Converts area readings from documents, surveys and geometry into acres, compares each pair, and gives an overall verdict using demo tolerances.
purpose: Shows whether recorded areas agree, so a reviewer knows where to look, without deciding which value is correct.
why: Likely reason: the app compares several sources, so one shared rule set gives the same answer everywhere.
how: The policy holds an identifier, a 2 percent limit for consistent, a 5 percent limit for review, and a disclaimer. A unit table gives the acre factor for each accepted unit name. The normalizeAreaToAcres function accepts only positive finite numbers with a known unit. The areaSource function adds the acre value and an availability flag. The compareParcelAreas function finds the absolute gap, the percentage gap relative to the larger value, and returns a status, or insufficient evidence when either reading is missing. The summarizeParcelAreaComparisons function turns the pairs into one overall verdict. The compareAllParcelAreas function runs the three pairs and the summary.
inputs: Area readings with a value, a unit, a source type and a reference.
outputs: Acre values, pairwise comparisons, an overall summary with a key and status, and the policy used.
risks: The cut-offs are demo values, not legal tolerances. The summary only recognises particular source combinations, so a new source type is ignored by it.
debug: If a verdict surprises you, check the acre value for each source first, then the percentage. If the summary is wrong, check the pair lookups use the right source type names.
